chapter: Small's Paradise, Fletcher Henderson and Horace
title: What Hawkins showed the tenor could do: depth, tone and running changes
summary: They contrast Hawkins's full tenor tone with light modern players who run changes without telling a story.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young

blocks.x: But it seems to me the way they play it is so -- it's just like a pale shadow of what somebody like Hawk or Johnny Hodges does on a saxophone, where they really fill the damn thing and --
I mean to me I don't -- I think that was a great --
The thing is that Hawk demonstrated what that instrument could do.

You can't tell me that what (unintelligible) gible) was getting out of it is the full potential of the instrument. I mean his ideas are fine and -- I mean it's -- even the sound he gets has a charm, but I think Hawk -- shows you what the instrument can do. (unintelligible).
If you've got the guts to do it.
Because (unintelligible) the horn the tenor requires the embellishment of depth, the depth of it, deepness of it.
And you take, for instance, like is so light it sounds recently a lot of these young fellows, the tone sounded like an alto almost.

I said that's not the tenor tone. When we had the jazz string I've told them fellows that (unintelligible), said, you should study more on your tone. You got an instrument which is actually taken up from the cello because cello is closer to human voice. They tell you that when you're going to school and learning music. I like to hear the cello anytime.
Yeah. Well, you can see in a way where Hawk's knowledge of that, I think, partly went into the
It did, right. I told them, I said, this horn requires depth and expression because if you're going to run, run, run, run, run, you're not saying anything.
Well, suppose they say, well, play me Tea for Two, give them a little idea of it. They ain't going to be playing no Tea for Two in no fast two-four.
Well, I mean it's -- the way they got onto that run changes was that it didn't really matter what the tune was --
-- anymore, did it? So the character of the music is just thrown away.
That's just to show off your virtuosity.
You don't tell a story anymore.
